public_rationale: The sentence is a hedged impression. Zitron says the AI that major tech companies are integrating 'doesn't actually seem to' do anything new, make a profit, or meet a need. 'Anything new' and 'any particular need' have no plain measure. 'Every major tech company' is not defined. The evidence gathered includes no AI-specific profit or loss figure for any company, so the profit part cannot be checked from this record. Some facts cut against the 'need' wording. CNBC reported that 7 percentage points of Azure growth in Microsoft's quarter ended March 31, 2024 were related to AI (e1). On April 25, 2024, Microsoft's CEO said GitHub Copilot had 1.8 million paid subscribers (e2). Revenue growth and paid subscribers are not profit, and they do not settle a subjective claim about novelty or need. So the claim is recorded as not adjudicable.
limitations: The evidence covers only Microsoft. It does not cover other major tech companies.
The evidence does not show whether any company disclosed AI-specific profit or loss in the first half of 2024.
A stricter reader could treat paid adoption as contradicting the 'need' part of the claim.
Revenue and subscriber figures do not show whether the AI features were profitable.
